messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: block-diagonal mass matrix?
parts:
Hi!

So far we have HMC with full mass matrix or diagonal mass matrix (and the diagonal version works a lot faster, I know). But what about block-diagonal mass-matrices? Maybe these would make sense in some applications?

For example, we often have varying parameters on some unit of interest. These individual parameters which are made specific in a hierachichal model to the unit of interest will always be correlated and hence a block in the mass matrix for these parameters would make sense.

Specifically, I am thinking about patients which are described by a set of parameters - those parameters which I fit with a hierarchical model specific to a patient will end up being correlated and hence a block for the patient-level would maybe make sense?

I know, identifying this structure from the model is another story...

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] block-diagonal mass matrix?
parts:
Nope, no way we could identify the structure from the model,
but there may be ways to identify it in practice if it truly
is block diagonal. It'd be nice to be able to do some kind
of sparse or low-rank approximation, which is a different angle
that could be combined with block-diagonal structure.

You'd need to toss the hierarchical parameters in, too, since those
are also correlated. And of course, if they all go in a regression,
then they'll be correlated with all the other regression parameters.

- Bob
